heading: When to use each
text:
### When to use each [LNOG.2.4]

| Goal | Dialect | Overrides |
|---|---|---|
| Hard RT with logical derived facts | `realtime` | — |
| Hard RT, no derived facts, smallest TMS cost | `realtime` | `logical: false` |
| Maximum simplicity, stream-only processing | `default` | `logical: false` |
| Stream-only, O(1) joins, O(1) retraction | `default` | `logical: false`, `linear_scan: false` |
| Tightest possible T_wcet — all guarantees | `realtime` | `linear_scan: false`, `logical: false` |

The rows that use the `realtime` dialect are deferred with it, and the
compiler refuses them in this edition ([LCAP.2.1.5]).

A combination that sets both `logical: false` and `linear_scan: false`
constrains the program to single-pattern rules that perform only
alpha-level tests ([LCAP.3.1]).  Every fact lifecycle is `explicit`,
`ttl`, `activation`, or `ambient`.  The retraction path has no TMS
lookup, no cascade, and no join index traversal.  This is the
theoretical floor for a Rete engine: pure alpha-network stream
processing.
